scope: Severity reconciliation only for 25 disagreements among 182 inherited P0/P1 findings; no raw finding edits, cross-unit dedup closure, or completion of remaining duplication units.
method: Compared both independent verdicts by source ID. Checked every reviewer-A cited path and cited line number against git show at the frozen commit; recorded the frozen blob SHA-256. Decision reasons use the cited source contracts and retain both reviewers' complete original evidence and limitations. This is a source-level review, not live failure reproduction.

disagreements.decision_reason: Malformed sensitive-port output is suppressed while a timed-out ID is retained. The downstream quota effect requires such output and retained state; this is a bounded diagnostics failure.

reviewer_a.reason: A retained sensitive id makes malformed lines on that port discardable until cleanup, before diagnostics receive them. The downstream quota consequence is conditional.
reviewer_a.limits: Frozen source review only; no live-provider or daemon incidence measurement.

reviewer_b.evidence: sensitive_responses.ex:87-100 falls back to retained_for_port? for any unmatched binary and does not remove retained IDs; await.ex:34-36 retains a timed-out sensitive request. This can suppress later malformed lines until cleanup.
reviewer_b.limitations: The downstream quota-misclassification consequence requires a qualifying provider banner and was not reproduced; severity is lower than the inherited P1 absent occurrence evidence.

disagreements.decision_reason: The queue pause paths omit the confirmation that disarms the armed five-second containment fallback. A deliberately paused worker can be reaped; the trigger is queue-turn pause, with no demonstrated irreversible loss.

reviewer_a.limits: Frozen source review only; reachability and incidence are not established beyond the stated code path.

reviewer_b.evidence: QueueDrain paused branches and pause-agent receives omit PauseContainment.confirm while TurnLoop confirms; the containment fallback is armed for paused Codex sessions. The five-second timer can reap a deliberately paused process group.
reviewer_b.limitations: Applies to the queue-drain pause paths, not every pause; exact timer execution was not reproduced.

disagreements.decision_reason: The stalled buffer is re-sent to the same mailbox only after the stalled cursor advances. A newer event already in that mailbox can advance the cursor first, then the older buffered event is discarded. This is a real event-loss path; the required transient stall plus interleaving and unknown downstream recovery keep the P0 impact claim unproven.

reviewer_a.reason: Buffered events are re-sent behind already queued mailbox events after cursor advance; a newer queued event can advance the cursor and cause buffered older events to be dropped. No live frequency measured.
reviewer_a.limits: Frozen source review only; reachability and incidence are not established beyond the stated code path.

reviewer_b.evidence: subscription_store.ex:375-393 drops IDs at/below cursor; retry_stalled at 398 onward resolves by re-sending buffered events to its own mailbox. Newer already-queued messages precede those sends and can move the cursor, silently discarding buffered events.
reviewer_b.limitations: Requires a transient stall and a newer event already queued; no live event-loss count was measured.
